title: Kinetic friction is a force that decelerates a sliding object
summary: OpenStax Physics says kinetic friction opposes sliding and makes a sliding object slow down.
body: OpenStax Physics says a sliding box decelerates because a net external force acts on it. The force it names is friction. Kinetic friction is a force from a surface, parallel to that surface, that opposes sliding and makes the object slow down. Static friction is the kind that stops slipping before motion starts. With an air-hockey table's air off, the page says, a puck travels only a short way before friction stops it. The account is the textbook's. It gives no friction number for a kitchen floor.

sources.title: OpenStax Physics, 4.2 Newton's First Law of Motion: Inertia
